prompts.bbt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished landscape 16:9 game cover for a minimal professional developer portfolio.
Create a polished editorial cover artwork for the actual student game BREAKNECK BATTLE TANK, grounded closely in the three supplied references.
Input images: image 1 is reference for the chunky green toy tank and purple toy turret designs, not an edit target; image 2 and image 3 are gameplay/environment/model references for a 3D top-down arcade shooter set in a child's tabletop toy battlefield.
Scene: a warm orange-tan tabletop arena with a few oversized wooden alphabet blocks, a simple toy rocket and book edges. Feature one compact green tank in a dynamic elevated three-quarter view, preserving the reference tank's simple toy hull, circular turret and chunky tracks; a purple toy turret and a smaller burgundy enemy tank behind it. Preserve the simple colorful low-poly game model identity. A small glow/spark from the green tank's damaged engine suggests its unstable core and race against time; restrained blue-purple projectile arcs suggest arcade movement.
Style: intentionally stylized promotional illustration with game-asset-like geometry, subtle paper grain, crisp silhouettes, warm lighting, professional art direction. Not realistic military hardware, not AAA game footage.
Composition: subject and all typography within central 80% of image, safely usable as a 16:10 card crop. Strong hierarchy and generous breathing space, readable at small card size. Integrate large off-white condensed uppercase sans-serif title over quiet darkened upper negative space; two lines reading exactly "BREAKNECK" then "BATTLE TANK". No other text. Typography feels refined and graphic, not a cluttered logo or explosive badge.
Avoid: menus, PLAY/OPTIONS/CREDITS, HUD, health bars, buttons, speech bubbles, extra slogans, brands, badges, watermark, photorealistic war, extra fictional machines. Generate one finished cover only, 16:9 landscape.
prompts.nexus:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished landscape 16:9 game cover for a minimal professional developer portfolio.
Create a polished cover artwork for TALE OF NEXUS: THE TRUE GUARDIAN using the actual environments in the three provided screenshots.
Input images: image 1 is environment reference showing a snowy pine forest, gray stone castle gate and weathered wizard/creature statues; image 2 is environment reference showing the circular stone portal crowned with a winged creature among snow, angular rocks and pine trees; image 3 is environment reference showing pale lavender stone platforms, gold-accented rails and a broad staircase climbing above a sea of cloud. They are visual references, not exact layouts to copy.
Scene/backdrop: combine the actual snowy Ground realm and cloudborne Sky realm into one coherent atmospheric landscape: the familiar circular carved stone portal in the lower midground, snowy pines and rocks framing it, with the pale lavender stair-and-platform route appearing through and beyond the portal above clouds. Keep the low-poly stylized stonework and game scenery recognizable from the screenshots. Suggest the quest's two artifacts using a modest slender sword and golden bow motif incorporated discreetly near the portal base; they must not dominate or imply a detailed character narrative.
Style: refined illustrated key art, restrained painterly treatment over recognizable supplied game geometry, soft wintry light, muted forest green/slate blue/lavender stone and subtle antique gold. Landscape-led rather than character-led. Do not invent photorealistic or high-budget game footage.
Composition: clean depth and a single focal portal, central 80% safe for 16:10 crop. Quiet dark upper center for readable cream typography at small card size. Title exactly "TALE OF NEXUS", elegant widely spaced uppercase serif; directly beneath, smaller subtitle exactly "THE TRUE GUARDIAN". Restrained professional title hierarchy, no ornate unreadable lettering.
Avoid: new hero characters, dragons, arbitrary grand castles, armies, UI, menus, HUD, extra slogans, brands, badges, watermark. One finished cover only, 16:9 landscape.
prompts.phase:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished landscape 16:9 game cover for a minimal professional developer portfolio.
Create a tasteful abstract architectural game cover for PHASE SWAP, a 14-day WHITEBOX puzzle demo. It must honestly retain the supplied prototype's visual identity.
Input images: all three images are references for the actual game blockout architecture, gray checkerboard walls/floors, simple cubic supports and ramps, solid magenta blocks and bridge slabs, and translucent cyan ghost blocks/bridges. Image 1 and 3 are broad room geometry references; image 2 clearly shows solid versus ghost block material. Use as reference, no need to copy HUD or camera.
Scene: compose a striking perspective of the actual simple gray checkerboard puzzle room using a few large blockout cube supports, a ramp and narrow intersecting bridge slabs. One solid magenta rectangular slab and one cyan translucent ghost slab form the main visual focus, showing two matter states with partial overlap. Ground surfaces remain visibly whitebox gray grid/checker material, geometry simple and untextured. Clear light transmission through the cyan object, opaque matte magenta counterpart. Omit mannequins to give the architecture and state mechanics visual focus.
Style: restrained architectural concept illustration/graphic key art based on whitebox game geometry, crisp forms, controlled contrast and atmospheric shadow, cool neutral gray with faithful cyan and magenta accents. Professional finished cover composition of an unfinished prototype, NOT a finished science-fiction environment. No photorealistic laboratory set dressing, no detailed machinery.
Composition: generous quiet upper area for title, architectural focus in lower/middle frame, every essential element central 80% safe for 16:10 cropping and strong readability in a small card. Large refined geometric uppercase sans-serif title exactly "PHASE SWAP", cream-white, with a subtle offset cyan/magenta edge that never compromises readability. Small widely spaced "DEMO" underneath. No other text.
Avoid: HUD, tutorial words, preview watermark, editor gizmos, menus, extra slogans, badges, brand logos, characters, weapons, pipes, shiny AAA sci-fi corridors, neon overload. One finished cover only, 16:9 landscape.
